Shoshone-Paiute Tribes

The Shoshone-Paiute Tribes are the joint government of the Duck Valley Indian Reservation, which spans Idaho and Nevada. The Tribes' history identifies Western Shoshone and Northern Paiute descendants in this community. Its public account, a historical constitution and a federal water-settlement statement offer a focused introduction to Duck Valley rather than all Shoshone or Paiute peoples.

These are selected starting points. The full annotated collection, source perspectives, inspection limits and remaining research questions follow below. A starting guide is not an exhaustive history or community endorsement.

01

Duck Valley’s community history

The Tribes' Cultural Department distinguishes the reservation's establishment in 1877 from expansions in 1886 and 1910. It recounts movement, schooling and resistance to a proposed relocation to Fort Hall. Its narrative keeps the shared Western Shoshone and Northern Paiute community visible. Undated membership and acreage totals are omitted here, and its account is attributed to the Tribes rather than presented as an independently reconstructed history.

Read the sources [1] Shoshone-Paiute Tribes of the Duck Valley Indian Reservation

02

Reading the 1936 constitution historically

A public transcription of the 1936 constitution and bylaws names the joint Tribes and sets out a business council, territorial jurisdiction, land provisions and an amendment process. Its certification distinguishes a March 21 ratification vote from April 20 approval. The transcription has apparent errors; neither it nor its original date establishes present citizenship rules or all later amendments.

Read the sources [2] 1936 Government Printing Office text transcribed by University of Oklahoma Native American Constitution and Law Digitization Project

03

Water settlement and a later proposal

The Interior Department's H.R. 1869 statement describes the 2009 Duck Valley water-rights settlement and a proposed correction about trust-fund interest. It places the reservation on both sides of the Idaho–Nevada border. This is a dated federal legislative position about one settlement issue, not the Tribes' full water history. The inspected statement does not establish subsequent enactment, implementation or present outcomes.

Read the sources [3] U.S. Department of the Interior, Secretary’s Indian Water Rights Office

Our History — Cultural Department ↗

The joint government identifies Western Shoshone and Northern Paiute descendants at Duck Valley and recounts reservation creation/expansion, resistance to relocation, schooling and constitutional organization. This is its institutional history, not a uniform history of all Northern Paiute communities. Undated membership and present-program figures are not used.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Complete visible history body, lines43–61, read October23. Linked history videos were not played and photographs not reused.

Review recorded: October 23, 2026

Government / historical primary legal document1936 Government Printing Office text transcribed by University of Oklahoma Native American Constitution and Law Digitization ProjectSource 2

Constitution and Bylaws of the Shoshone-Paiute Tribes of the Duck Valley Reservation, approved April20,1936 ↗

Historical governing instrument identifying the joint Tribes, territorial jurisdiction, council powers, land provisions and amendment process. Its adoption certification dates the vote to March21,1936 and approval to April20. The transcription contains apparent errors; do not silently correct its text or present 1936 provisions as verified current law.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Complete HTML transcription including constitution articlesI–X, bylawsI–VI and adoption/approval certification, lines53–266. Original scan and amendments not inspected.

Review recorded: October 23, 2026

Government / primary congressional statementU.S. Department of the Interior, Secretary’s Indian Water Rights OfficeSource 3

H.R.1869 — statement on Duck Valley water-rights settlement technical correction ↗

Federal account of the joint Tribes’ Idaho/Nevada water-rights settlement and a proposed trust-fund interest correction. Useful for separating the 2009 settlement from a later legislative proposal. The Department’s support is a policy position, not proof of enactment or successful implementation.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Complete statement for the record, lines34–65. Bill enactment, later implementation and underlying settlement instruments not independently reviewed.

Review recorded: October 23, 2026
